item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers placed pitcher Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list on Sunday, which means he could miss his final regular-season turn in the rotation next week.
Skubal's next start is scheduled for Friday against the San Francisco Giants, which could fall within the three-to-seven days that players are allowed to be away from the team while on the bereavement list. But Dodgers manager Dave Roberts appeared to believe that Skubal will be back by Friday, telling reporters he would miss "a couple days."
"Some personal stuff going on, but he's fine," Roberts said, via MLB.com's Sonja Chen.
Skubal pitched in Saturday's 10-4 win over the Giants, allowing four runs and eight hits over five innings. He walked two batters with three strikeouts, tying his lowest total of the season. Saturday's game was the first time Skubal gave up more than three runs in his nine starts with the Dodgers. according to The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya.
Tarik Skubal pitched five innings and allowed four runs but is grateful for the offensive support.
“Yeah, no doubt. Obviously, I wasn't very good today, but the offense and defense and bullpen picked me up big time, and that's what good teams do,” Skubal said. “You know, they… pic.twitter.com/4TUdrQqgH8
"Obviously, I wasn't very good today, but the offense and defense and bullpen picked me up big time, and that's what good teams do," Skubal said after the game.
In his nine starts with the Dodgers since being acquired from the Detroit Tigers before the MLB trade deadline, Skubal has a 2.95 ERA and 4-2 record with 60 strikeouts in 55 innings.
The Dodgers took a 2-0 lead on a first-inning RBI double by Max Muncy and Mookie Betts hitting a run-scoring single in the second. But San Francisco tied the score in the third on a 2-run homer from Victor Bericoto, hitting a fastball left in the very middle of the strike zone by Skubal.
The two teams then traded runs during the third through fifth innings, resulting in a 4-4 tie, before the Dodgers pulled away on a 2-run hit by Tommy Edman and RBI single from Miguel Rojas. In the following inning, the Dodgers added three more runs with Will Smith driving in a run and Josue De Paula hitting a 2-run single.
To fill Skubal's spot on the active roster, Emmet Sheehan was recalled from Triple-A Oklahoma City. He pitched 5 1/3 scoreless innings with one hit allowed and nine strikeouts, taking over for opener Jack Dreyer in the Dodgers' 3-1 win. In his previous two starts before being optioned, Sheehan allowed one run over 11 2/3 innings with 15 strikeouts.

Sheehan, de 26 años, lanzó seis entradas en blanco contra los Marlins el domingo pasado y lleva marca de 5-8 con el equipo de Los Ángeles en el 2026, registrando una marca personal de 22 aperturas, ha recetado 123 ponches en 107.0 entradas y WHIP de 1.21. Se encuentra en su tercera campaña con los Dodgers, registrando efectividad de 4.23 con récord de 15-12 en 50 presentaciones (45 aperturas). Fue elegido por los Dodgers en la sexta ronda del Draft del 2021 desde Boston College.
Hurt, de 28 años, regresa para su quinta estadía con el equipo. Tiene marca de 4-1 con efectividad de 4.33 este año y 56 ponches en 43.2 entradas. Ha estado con los Dodgers durante tres temporadas, acumulando efectividad de 3.78 con 62 ponches en 52.1 entradas y marca de 4-2. Fue elegido originalmente por los Marlins en la quinta ronda del Draft del 2020 desde la Universidad del Sur de California (USC).
Halvorsen, de 26 años, realizó una presentación el sábado, lanzando un episodio en blanco con dos ponches. Realizó 11 presentaciones con los Dodgers, alcanzando foja de 1-1 con efectividad de 8.10. Antes de integrarse a los Dodgers, lanzó en 21 partido por los Rockies este año, registrando marca de 0-1 con efectividad de 4.74. Lleva 86 presentaciones en las Grandes Ligas por los Rockies (2024-2026) y los Dodgers (2026), y tiene foja de 4-5 con efectividad de 4.78 y 72 ponches en 81.0 capítulos. Fue seleccionado en la séptima ronda del Draft del 2023 por los Rockies desde la Universidad de Tennessee.
Skubal, de 29 años, lanzó el sábado, concediendo cuatro carreras en cinco innings. Ha realizado nueve aperturas por los bicampeones desde que fue adquirido desde los Tigres y tiene marca de 4-2 con efectividad de 2.95 en 55 capítulos. En la temporada, lleva 11-7 con efectividad de 2.85 en 25 salidas. El dos veces ganador del Premio Cy Young tiene siete años de experiencia en la Gran Carpa, acumulando marca de 65-44 con efectividad de 3.04 en 162 presentaciones (159 como abridor). Lleva 1,065 ponches en 918.1 entradas con WHIP de 1.02. Fue elegido por los Tigres en la novena ronda del Draft del 2018 desde la Universidad de Seattle.

item.title: [presstelegram.com] Dodgers’ Dave Roberts trying to find ‘balance’ as Freddie Freeman struggles to rediscover his swing
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Dave Roberts has a dilemma. Never one to accept days off as the answer to anything, Freeman would probably benefit from some downtime this week – but he also needs at-bats to rediscover the swing that had him batting .300 for the season just two weeks ago or recalibrate it to accommodate his balky knee. “There’s rest,
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Dave Roberts has a dilemma.
His first baseman, Freddie Freeman, just turned 37 years old and has been slumping badly down the stretch while playing through patellar tendinitis in his right knee. Never one to accept days off as the answer to anything, Freeman would probably benefit from some downtime this week – but he also needs at-bats to rediscover the swing that had him batting .300 for the season just two weeks ago or recalibrate it to accommodate his balky knee.
“There’s rest, but there’s also trying to find your swing,” Roberts acknowledged after putting Freeman in the lineup on Saturday and Sunday – a day game following a night game.
“I think it’s a work in progress,” Roberts said of Freeman’s swing. “The other day in Cincinnati (a three-hit game on Tuesday), I think it was looking pretty good, and then. I actually thought yesterday there were a couple good swings there.
“Obviously, the results weren’t there for him, and he’s frustrated, and I think that you just kind of have to count on him to figure it out and bet on him. And that’s kind of where we’re at. But again, having the week off (with a first-round bye) would be huge too.”
Freeman said he has been doing some different drills in the batting cage, focused on hitting the ball “out front” more.
“I feel like my faults are I try to hit the ball to the opposite field too much, and I let the ball get too deep, and it caused me to slide,” Freeman said earlier this week. “So today (in the cage) was – foot down early, catch the ball out front a little bit.”
Even with that three-hit game in Cincinnati and a two-hit game on Thursday, Freeman went into Sunday just 6 for his past 48 (.125), hitless in nine at-bats in the first two games of the series with the Giants.
“Got to go for results-based things right now,” Freeman said. “Looking to be hot for a few weeks. That’s all I’m trying to do.
“I’m just trying to find something that gives me results. We’re at the time where we’re just trying to get hot for five weeks here. So kind of like I did in the World Series a couple years ago (when his ankle was injured), I did the step-out move. That’s not sustainable over six months. I’m not trying to find something that’s sustainable. I’m trying to find something that works for four weeks.”
OHTANI WORK
The “hope” is that Shohei Ohtani will be ready to come off the injured list when he is eligible on Wednesday, Roberts said. When he does, Roberts expects him to be in the lineup for the final five games.
“Absolutely,” Roberts said. “Yeah, he’ll need those live at-bats.”
Roberts has said Ohtani is “pain-free” but he acknowledged that Ohtani won’t be feeling 100% when he returns – but will be closer to it than he has been in weeks.
“Discomfort you can play through,” Roberts said of how Ohtani is feeling. “I think there’s a difference between discomfort and pain. Is it 100%? Probably not. Is it better than it was a week ago? Yes.
“Honestly I think that’s just a better question for Shohei to give more specifics, but I do think that when he’s activated it’s going to be the best physical place he’s been in in quite some time.”
Ohtani has spoken with the media just once in the past five weeks (before he went on the IL).
KIM CALL
Signed to a three-year, $12.5 million contract, South Korean infielder Hyeseong Kim has spent most of the second season of that contract in Triple-A where he hit .265 with a .682 OPS in 84 games. He hasn’t been up with the Dodgers since May but Roberts said Kim will be part of the “conversation” for the postseason roster.
“My expectation is Hyeseong will be here during the off week (next week) and potentially be a conversation for the postseason (roster) because he has the ability to run, to play defense, and steal a base,” Roberts said. “He’s in the conversation, yes.”
Kim was on the postseason roster last fall, appearing in just two games. It will be difficult to give him a spot on a bench that seems set with Alex Call, Hunter Feduccia, Miguel Rojas, Kiké Hernandez and Josue De Paula.
ROSTER MOVES
The Dodgers placed pitcher Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list on Sunday and recalled Emmet Sheehan from Triple-A to pitch ‘bulk’ in Sunday’s game.
Also, reliever Seth Halvorsen was returned to Triple-A and reliever Kyle Hurt was recalled.
Sheehan is still under consideration for a bullpen role on the postseason roster.
UP NEXT
The Dodgers are off on Monday.
Padres (TBA) at Dodgers (TBA), Tuesday, 7:10 p.m., SportsNet LA, 570 AM

item.content:encoded:
LOS ÁNGELES -- El dicho asegura que el pitcheo gana campeonatos, y eso fue cierto de distintas maneras cuando los Dodgers conquistaron Series Mundiales consecutivas en 2024 y 2025.
Los Dodgers de 2024 tuvieron que apoyarse mucho en su bullpen por necesidad, mientras que el equipo de 2025 se respaldó en su rotación para defender con éxito el título, a tal punto que sus cuatro abridores lanzaron en el decisivo Juego 7.
Mientras los Dodgers buscan un tricampeonato este año, volverán a depender de sus cuatro abridores, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell y Tyler Glasnow, para marcar la pauta. Pero su bullpen parece menos inestable que el año pasado y podría ser uno de los grupos con mayor flexibilidad mientras Los Ángeles evalúa cómo conformar sus rosters para la postemporada.
Los Dodgers pudieron observar a varios candidatos para el bullpen de playoffs al ejecutar con éxito un juego de bullpen la tarde del domingo en el Dodger Stadium, completando una barrida de tres encuentros sobre los Gigantes con una victoria por 3-1. El derecho Emmet Sheehan ponchó a nueve en 5.1 innings en blanco como relevista largo, dándole a Los Ángeles otra interesante alternativa para la postemporada.
La cuarta victoria consecutiva de los Dodgers mantuvo su ventaja de cuatro juegos sobre los Bravos por el segundo mejor récord de la Liga Nacional, y el descanso en la primera ronda de la postemporada que viene con esa posición, cuando restan seis juegos por disputar.

item.title: [MLB.com] How Sheehan, Sasaki and others look to fit in LA's postseason 'pen plans

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- The saying goes that pitching wins championships, and that was true in different ways when the Dodgers won back-to-back World Series in 2024 and '25.
The 2024 Dodgers had to lean heavily on their bullpen out of necessity, while the '25 team rode its rotation to a successful title defense -- so much so that all four starting pitchers took the ball in the winner-take-all Game 7.
As the Dodgers go for a three-peat this year, they'll once again look for their starting four of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow to set the tone. But their bullpen feels less volatile than it was last year, and it could be one of the most fluid position groups as L.A. considers how to piece together its postseason rosters.
One way or another, the Dodgers will carry their best 13 pitchers in the postseason, because as manager Dave Roberts has said repeatedly, like a mantra: "Every inning in the postseason is leverage."
The Dodgers got a look at several postseason 'pen candidates when they ran a bullpen game to success on Sunday afternoon at Dodger Stadium, capping a three-game sweep of the Giants with a 3-1 victory. Right-hander Emmet Sheehan struck out nine in 5 1/3 scoreless innings of bulk relief, giving L.A. an intriguing option to add to the mix.
The Dodgers' fourth straight victory maintained their four-game lead over the Braves for the second-best record in the National League -- and a first-round postseason bye -- with six games left to play.
The greatest need in the bullpen is right-handed leverage arms. Edwin Díaz, who signed a three-year, $69 million deal to be their closer, has been relegated to lower leverage for the time being amid his poor performance in an injury-ravaged season. Edgardo Henriquez, who stepped up to become L.A.'s most reliable righty in leverage, is out for the rest of the regular season due to a lower back strain. He could return during the postseason, but the uncertainty still creates a need.
Evan Phillips and Brock Stewart have been solid options, but they have been more valuable as part of the bridge to the ninth inning, rather than to close out games. In order to find such options from the right-hand side, the Dodgers can turn to the strength of their staff: the rotation.
Sheehan is one candidate, although he'll remain stretched out through the end of the regular season as rotation depth. Another is Roki Sasaki, who was also originally going to remain built up as a starter upon his return from the 15-day IL. Instead, Roberts said, Sasaki will likely be activated Tuesday and be available out of the bullpen, beginning his transition to relief in the final days of the regular season.
"He's done it. He's really good. He's a neutral pitcher, high-octane stuff," Roberts said. "You really just need four starters, you know. So we're in a good spot there for now."
Sheehan and Sasaki both got a crash course in short-burst relief last fall. While Sasaki thrived as the Dodgers' postseason closer, Sheehan was scored on in his first four appearances before rebounding for scoreless outings in Games 3 and 7 of the World Series.
For Sheehan, adapting his typical routine to relief was difficult, but he believes that he can build on last year if he gets the call to the 'pen again.
"Having that experience helps a lot," Sheehan said. "Just getting back into that, I know what I need to do to get ready to go into the game."
And don't count out Díaz. His pitch to earn a spot in the postseason 'pen began with two scoreless innings against the Giants this weekend.
When the postseason comes, the Dodgers may not be able to avoid using Díaz in leverage, even if they don't throw him into a comparable situation in the final days of the regular season. But if he shows enough this week, then L.A. will bet on his track record.
"I gotta show them I’m part of that bullpen," Díaz said. "I haven’t pitched [much] this year, and when I’ve been on the mound I’ve been struggling. So right now, I’m giving my 200% just to show them I will be in that roster spot."

item.title: [The Sporting Tribune] Dodgers get strong outings from Sheehan and Bubic in 3-1 win

item.description: LOS ANGELES -- Before Sunday’s game, the Los Angeles Dodgers made several roster moves, recalling right-handed pitchers Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt while optioning right-hander Seth Halvorsen. The club also placed left-hander Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list. The Dodgers would go on to win 3-1, with Kris Bubic recording the victory for his fourth win of the season. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- Before Sunday’s game, the Los Angeles Dodgers made several roster moves, recalling right-handed pitchers Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt while optioning right-hander Seth Halvorsen. The club also placed left-hander Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list.
The Dodgers would go on to win 3-1, with Kris Bubic recording the victory for his fourth win of the season.
Giants rookie starter Matt Wilkinson kept the Dodgers in check for most of his outing, pitching five shutout innings while striking out six. He consistently kept the Dodgers’ lineup off balance and prevented them from generating much offensively.
For the Dodgers, however, the pitching staff put together a complete performance outside of the one run allowed by Jack Dreyer. Sheehan followed Dreyer and delivered an especially effective outing in his return to the roster.
The right-hander pitched 5.1 innings, allowing just one hit while striking out eight. Considering the struggles Sheehan has endured throughout the 2026 season, seeing him throw the ball this effectively was particularly encouraging after the many setbacks he has faced.
The outing also builds on what Sheehan did in his previous appearance on Sept. 13 against the Miami Marlins. He pitched six scoreless innings while striking out five before being optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City the following day. The Dodgers recalled him Sunday, and he immediately followed that previous performance with another strong showing.
It wasn’t until the sixth inning that the Dodgers finally got on the board. Tommy Edman hit a solo home run to right field, and Kiké Hernández followed with an RBI double in the seventh to give the Dodgers a 2-1 lead. The Dodgers would add additional insurance in the eighth when Max Muncy delivered an RBI single to give the Dodgers their final run of the game and a 3-1 lead.
Bubic also made an appearance, marking his second game with the Dodgers and his first at Dodger Stadium. He took over for Sheehan after the first out of the sixth inning and recorded the final two outs, striking out one of the two batters he faced.
Bubic, an All-Star in 2025, joined the Dodgers after being acquired at the trade deadline in August. Previously with the Kansas City Royals, Bubic carved out a role as one of the better left-handed starters in the American League while also proving capable of working out of the bullpen throughout his career.
That versatility is exactly what the Dodgers hope he can provide. The expectation is that Bubic could serve as a high-leverage reliever out of the bullpen once October arrives. His role could look similar to the one Justin Wrobleski had during the Dodgers’ 2025 playoff push, when Wrobleski was used as a reliever capable of covering multiple innings while remaining an effective arm.
Those plans have yet to be finalized, but Bubic’s previous experience gives the Dodgers another option to consider. The hope is that he can provide some stability to the bullpen during the final weeks of the regular season before the Dodgers determine their postseason roster.

Las cuatro transacciones involucraron a lanzadores de los Dodgers. También llamaron de vuelta a Kyle Hurt, colocaron a Tarik Skubal en la lista de duelo y enviaron a Seth Halvorsen a Triple-A Oklahoma City. Movimientos en el roste
item.content:encoded:
Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles llamaron de vuelta al lanzador Emmet Sheehan como parte de una serie de movimientos en el roster el domingo, y está previsto que el derecho se encargue de la mayor parte del juego en el cierre de la serie contra los Gigantes de San Francisco.
Las cuatro transacciones involucraron a lanzadores de los Dodgers. También llamaron de vuelta a Kyle Hurt, colocaron a Tarik Skubal en la lista de duelo y enviaron a Seth Halvorsen a Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Movimientos en el roster de los Dodgers
Jack Dreyer abrirá mientras los Dodgers buscan la barrida ante sus rivales del Área de la Bahía, antes de cederle el turno a Sheehan.
"Hoy estamos armando esto un poco con las opciones disponibles. Creo que se trata más de lo que, en nuestra opinión, le da a Emmet la mejor oportunidad", comentó el mánager Dave Roberts.
El jardinero derecho Kyle Tucker no estará en la alineación después de salir de la victoria del sábado por 10-4 debido a un lanzamiento foul que le pegó en la rodilla derecha.
Lesiones y esperanzas de regreso
Los Dodgers esperan ver pronto de regreso a Shohei Ohtani tras su primera estancia en la lista de lesionados desde que se unió al equipo en 2024. Podría ocurrir durante una serie de tres juegos contra los San Diego Padres que comienza la noche del martes. "Aún está en el aire, pero esa es nuestra esperanza", señaló Roberts.
Ohtani está en la lista de lesionados de 15 días por una inflamación en el bíceps derecho. También ha estado lidiando con molestias en la rodilla izquierda desde hace meses.
Expectativas sobre el regreso de Ohtani
Roberts cree que Ohtani llegará sin dolor a la última semana de la temporada regular, mientras los Dodgers presionan para asegurar un descanso y evitar la ronda de comodines.
"Creo que hay una diferencia entre molestia y dolor. ¿Está al 100 por ciento? Probablemente no. ¿Está mejor que hace una semana? Sí", manifestó Roberts.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers made a number of pitching moves ahead of Sunday’s series finale against the San Francisco Giants. Tarik Skubal, who started on Saturday, was placed on bereavement leave, which facilitated the return of Emmet Sheehan from Triple-A Oklahoma City. In addition, reliever Kyle Hurt was recalled and Seth Halvorsen optioned in a swap of right-handers in the bullpen.
Sheehan was just optioned on Monday and normally would have needed to stay in the minors for 15 days, but because he’s replacing a player on the bereavement list (or injured list or paternity list) that allows the right-hander to return early.
After getting sent down to Triple-A on August 3, Sheehan turned his season around, including winning Pacific Coast League pitcher of the month, and he allowed one run in 11 2/3 innings last week for the Dodgers before getting optioned to Oklahoma City so the Dodgers could use a fresh arm. In his last five outings — three in Triple-A, two with Dodgers — Sheehan has allowed only two runs in 29 innings with 39 strikeouts (36.4-percent strikeout rate) against only eight walks.
All 26 outings by Sheehan this season have been starts, but on Sunday he’ll follow an opener in left-hander Jack Dreyer. Sunday provides at least a practice run of Sheehan’s most likely role in the postseason, pitching in bulk relief.
“Emmet’s a part of the conversation,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday, “but if there is a role in the postseason it would be out of the ’pen.”
Bereavement leave lasts for a minimum of three days and up to seven, so Skubal wouldn’t be activated until Wednesday at the earliest. But considering the left-hander just started on Saturday, don’t expect him to be activated until his start day, likely next weekend in San Francisco.
Halvorsen has allowed nine runs in 10 innings with the Dodgers, including three home runs, with six strikeouts and two walks. He pitched a scoreless inning on Saturday, which was his third appearance in four days.
Hurt pitched a scoreless inning for Oklahoma City on Friday, his only appearance in the last week. Since getting optioned on September 5, Hurt pitched in three games for Oklahoma City, all scoreless innings. This season with the Dodgers, Hurt has a 4.33 ERA and 3.84 xERA in 43 games, with 56 strikeouts and 23 walks in 43 2/3 innings.
Saturday was his 15th day on optional assignment in Triple-A, making Sunday his first day eligible to return from the minors.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — The Los Angeles Dodgers recalled pitcher Emmet Sheehan as part of a series of roster moves Sunday, with the right-hander set to handle the bulk of their series finale against the San Francisco Giants.
All four transactions involved Dodgers pitchers. They also recalled Kyle Hurt, placed Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list and optioned Seth Halvorsen to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Jack Dreyer will start as the Dodgers go for the sweep against their Bay Area rivals before giving way to Sheehan, who is 5-8 with a 4.79 ERA in 22 games this season.
“Kind of piecing through the available options today,” manager Dave Roberts said. “I think it's just more of what gives Emmet, in our opinion, the best chance.”
Right fielder Kyle Tucker won't be in the lineup after coming out of Saturday's 10-4 victory because of a fouled pitch that went off his right knee. The early exit was described as precautionary, and Roberts felt it was worth giving him a day off, particularly with Tucker finding his stride after an erratic first season in Los Angeles. He is batting .429 with five homers, eight extra-base hits and 11 RBIs in his past 10 games.
The Dodgers expect to see Shohei Ohtani back soon after his first stint on the injured list since joining the team in 2024. It could come during a three-game series against the San Diego Padres that starts Tuesday night. “Still up in the air, but that’s our hope,” Roberts said.
Ohtani is on the 15-day IL with right biceps inflammation. He also has been dealing with left knee soreness for months.
Roberts believes Ohtani will be pain-free going into the last week of the regular season, with the Dodgers pushing to secure a bye to avoid the wild-card round.
“I think there's a difference between discomfort and pain,” Roberts said. “Is it 100%? Probably not. Is it better than it was a week ago? Yes. Honestly, I think that's just a better question for Shohei to give specifics. But I do think that when he's activated, it's going to be the best physical place he's been in in quite some time.”

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal is going on the bereavement list, manager Dave Roberts announced on Sunday.
The move came a day after Skubal suffered his worst start with the Dodgers, giving up four runs in five innings in Saturday’s 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants.
In his absence, Emmet Sheehan was called up from triple-A, returning in hopes of building off back-to-back strong starts earlier this month. He will follow opener Jack Dreyer on Sunday as the bulk pitcher for the Dodgers’ series finale with the Giants.
Roberts said Skubal would be away from the Dodgers for “a couple days.” No further information on his situation was available.
Skubal is a contender to be the Dodgers’ Game 1 starter in the playoffs, after being acquired in a blockbuster deal at the trade deadline in August. Even after Saturday’s setback, in which he allowed eight hits and bemoaned his lack of fastball command, the left-hander is 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA in nine starts with the Dodgers this season.
The two-time Cy Young Award winner will anchor a postseason rotation also expected to include Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tyler Glasnow and Blake Snell (assuming he continues to recover from his recent groin injury).
The Dodgers also freshened up their bullpen on Sunday, swapping out right-handers was calling up Kyle Hurt and optioning Seth Halvorsen.
The team enters Sunday with the chance to not only sweep the Giants, but further lower their current magic number of four to secure a first-round bye in the playoffs.
They enter play on Sunday four games ahead of the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed in the National League.

item.content:encoded:
Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles anunciaron varios movimientos en su cuerpo de lanzadores. El equipo colocó al zurdo Tarik Skubal en la lista de duelo, llamó a los derechos Emmet Sheehan y Kyle Hurt, y envió a Seth Halvorsen a las Ligas Menores.
El comunicado no ofreció detalles sobre la situación familiar de Skubal ni una fecha específica para su regreso.
El zurdo de 29 años viene de permitir cuatro carreras en cinco entradas durante su presentación de anoche. Desde que fue adquirido procedente de los Tigres de Detroit, ha realizado nueve aperturas con los Dodgers, con récord de 4-2 y efectividad de 2.95 en 55 innings.
En toda la temporada, Skubal acumula balance de 11-7 y promedio de carreras limpias de 2.85 en 25 aperturas. El ganador de dos premios Cy Young ha sido una pieza importante del pitcheo de Los Ángeles desde su llegada.
Emmet Sheehan regresa después de una salida dominante
Sheehan, de 26 años, lanzó seis entradas sin permitir carreras frente a los Marlins el pasado domingo. El derecho suma 22 aperturas esta temporada, la mayor cantidad de su carrera, y presenta récord de 5-8.
En 107 entradas ha ponchado a 123 bateadores y mantiene un WHIP de 1.21. Está en su tercera campaña con los Dodgers, organización que lo seleccionó en la sexta ronda del Draft de 2021, procedente de Boston College.
Su regreso le ofrece al equipo un brazo que viene de responder con una actuación dominante ante Miami.
Kyle Hurt recibe otra oportunidad con el equipo grande
Kyle Hurt también fue llamado y comienza su quinta estancia de la temporada con los Dodgers. El derecho de 28 años tiene marca de 4-1, efectividad de 4.33 y 56 ponches en 43 entradas y dos tercios durante esta campaña.
En sus tres temporadas con Los Ángeles acumula promedio de carreras limpias de 3.78, con 62 ponches en 52 entradas y un tercio.
Hurt fue seleccionado originalmente por los Marlins en la quinta ronda del Draft de 2020, procedente de la Universidad del Sur de California.
Seth Halvorsen baja a las menores
Por su parte, Halvorsen fue enviado a las Ligas Menores después de lanzar una entrada sin carreras y ponchar a dos bateadores anoche.
Aunque respondió en su presentación más reciente, el derecho de 26 años registra efectividad de 8.10 en 11 apariciones con los Dodgers, con una victoria y una derrota.
Antes de incorporarse a Los Ángeles, había participado en 21 encuentros con los Rockies de Colorado durante esta temporada, con marca de 0-1 y efectividad de 4.74.
Con estos movimientos, los Dodgers incorporan a Sheehan y Hurt como alternativas para su cuerpo de lanzadores mientras Skubal permanece en la lista de duelo.
Fuente: comunicado de prensa de Los Angeles Dodgers.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Dodgers make pair of roster moves to add pitchers before bullpen game
item.dc:creator: Blake Williams
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers recalled Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt, optioned Seth Halvorsen and placed Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list ahead of their series finale against the San Francisco Giants. Skubal and Halvorsen both pitched on Saturday in the victory. Skubal allowed four runs in five innings, showing a lot of frustration with his outing. He gave up eight hits and walked two while only striking out three. He has made nine starts for the Dodgers since being acquired from the Detroit Tigers
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers recalled Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt, optioned Seth Halvorsen and placed Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list ahead of their series finale against the San Francisco Giants.
Skubal and Halvorsen both pitched on Saturday in the victory.
Skubal allowed four runs in five innings, showing a lot of frustration with his outing. He gave up eight hits and walked two while only striking out three.
He has made nine starts for the Dodgers since being acquired from the Detroit Tigers and he is 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA in 55 innings. On the season, he is 11-7 with a 2.85 ERA in 25 starts.
The two-time Cy Young award winner has been in the Major Leagues seven seasons, posting a 65-44 record with a 3.04 ERA in 162 games (159 starts). He has 1,065 strikeouts in 918.1 innings while owning a 1.02 WHIP.
Skubal must be on the bereavement list for a minimum of three days and a maximum of seven days. It’s unclear why he was placed on bereavement leave, but the list is used if the player has a death or serious illness in their family.
Halvorsen tossed a scoreless inning with two strikeouts to close out Saturday’s game.
He made 11 appearances with the Dodgers, going 1-1 with an 8.10 ERA. Before joining the Dodgers, he appeared in 21 games for the Colorado Rockies this year, posting an 0-1 record with a 4.74 ERA.
He has made 86 Major League appearances for the Rockies (2024-26) and Dodgers (2026), and he is 4-5 with a 4.78 ERA and 72 strikeouts in 81 innings.
Dodgers add reinforcements for bullpen game
Sheehan returns after pitching six scoreless innings against the Miami Marlins last Sunday. He has gone 5-8 with the Dodgers in 2026, posting a career-high 22 starts, racking up 123 strikeouts in 107 innings and a 1.21 WHIP.
He is in his third season with the Dodgers, recording a 4.23 ERA with a 15-12 record in 50 games (45 starts).
The Dodgers needed a pitcher who could throw the bulk of the game on Sunday, and Sheehan is likely to fulfill that role.
Hurt returns for his fifth stint with the team and provides them with another fresh arm before the bullpen game. He has gone 4-1 with a 4.33 ERA this season and 56 strikeouts in 43.2 innings.
He has been with the Dodgers three seasons, compiling a 3.78 ERA with 62 strikeouts in 52.1 innings and a 4-2 mark.

item.title: [MLB.com] Skubal to bereavement list, Sheehan recalled among LA moves; Tucker out of lineup
item.dc:creator: Sonja Chen
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers made a flurry of roster moves before Sunday afternoon's series finale against the Giants, placing left-hander Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list, recalling right-handers Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt from Triple-A Oklahoma City and optioning right-hander Seth Halvorsen. Manager Dave Roberts does not think the soreness
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers made a flurry of roster moves before Sunday afternoon's series finale against the Giants, placing left-hander Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list, recalling right-handers Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt from Triple-A Oklahoma City and optioning right-hander Seth Halvorsen.
The Dodgers also gave right fielder Kyle Tucker Sunday off after he fouled a ball off the lower knee/upper shin area on his right leg on Saturday night. Manager Dave Roberts does not think the soreness will become an ongoing issue for Tucker, who is expected back in the lineup on Tuesday.
Here's how these moves will impact the Dodgers on Sunday and beyond:
Skubal will be away from the team for "a couple days," Roberts said. Players may spend between three to seven days on the bereavement list, so Skubal might not miss his next start, which is projected to come on Friday in San Francisco.
"Some personal stuff going on," Roberts said, "but he's fine."
Skubal is 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA in nine starts since being dealt to L.A. ahead of the Trade Deadline.
Sheehan was set to pitch bulk innings on Sunday behind opener Jack Dreyer. The thought was that pitching Sheehan behind an opener could not only help him get deeper into the game, but also prepare him for a possible bullpen role in the postseason, which would be his only path to making the roster.
In his previous two starts for the Dodgers, Sheehan allowed one earned run across 11 2/3 innings. After a strong stint in Triple-A, he has looked to trend in the right direction in what has been an inconsistent season overall (5-8, 4.79 ERA).
Tucker has heated up at the end of the first season of his four-year, $240 million contract, which has been disappointing (his .728 OPS is on track to be a career-worst mark in a full season). Since Sept. 9, he's hitting 15-for-35 (.429) with five home runs and 35 total bases, his most in a 10-game span this season.
On Saturday, Tucker exited the game after six innings due to a combination of the hit-by-pitch and the lopsided score. He said he feels fine, but Roberts decided to give him an extra day to rest after Tucker had played the previous nine games without a day off.
"I feel like everyone's grinding at this point in the season," Tucker said. "But I'll be good with it."

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers starter Tarik Skubal moved to the bereavement list on Sunday, and will be there for a "couple of days," per Dave Roberts.
In corresponding moves, the Dodgers optioned Seth Halvorsen and recalled Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt.
BREAKING: Tarik Skubal will be away from the Dodgers for a couple days due to personal reasons ?
Seth Halvorsen has also been optioned and Kyle Hurt and Emmet Sheehan are back.
Skubal last pitched for the Dodgers on Saturday, and had a frustrating outing—his worst since donning a Dodgers uniform. He lasted just five innings, allowing four earned runs on eight hits while recording a season-low three strikeouts.
What Does Tarik Skubal's Absence Mean?
The left-hander's presence on the bereavement list doesn't impact the rest of the Dodgers' season, as he will likely be ready for his next turn through the rotation if he stays out for a couple of days as Roberts said.
That should be a huge relief for the Dodgers, who have quite a few injuries among their starters as the postseason nears. Shohei Ohtani, Roki Sasaki and Eric Lauer are all on the IL, leaving LA with limited options.
An injury or extended period of absence for any of their remaining starters would throw a wrench in their plans for the postseason.
Additionally, Skubal's track record since joining the team is fantastic—serving as one of their best starters since the beginning of August. He has a 2.95 ERA through nine starts, striking out 60 batters through 55 innings pitched.
What Roles Will Kyle Hurt and Emmet Sheehan Play?
Hurt and Sheehan are likely to jump straight into the action, as the Dodgers are running a bullpen game on Sunday.
Jack Dreyer is getting the start, but using Hurt and Sheehan—both of whom have experience handling bulk innings—afterwards is the Dodgers' most likely move.
The duo have bounced between Triple-A and MLB over the past few weeks, but could very well find a spot on the team if they perform well Sunday. Sheehan is in the midst of a fantastic run of form, and has capitalized on both of his MLB opportunities in Setpember.
He only allowed one earned run through 11.2 innings pitched over his last two starts, and is a real candidate to make the postseason roster despite his recent stays in the minors.
Before that, though, he'll have to perform in Sunday's game against the Giants, which begins at 1:10 p.m. PT.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Tarik Skubal Away From Team as Dodgers Call Up Emmet Sheehan in Massive 4-Player Roster Move
item.dc:creator: Noah Camras; Unknown
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers announced a major roster move ahead of Sunday's series finale against the San Francisco Giants. The Dodgers have recalled right-handed pitchers Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt from Triple-A. Sheehan will take down bulk innings on Sunday as LA looks to preserve the bullpen heading into the final week of the regular season. As for the corresponding moves, left-handed pitcher Tarik Skubal was placed on the bereavement list and will be away from the team for "a couple days," per
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers announced a major roster move ahead of Sunday's series finale against the San Francisco Giants.
The Dodgers have recalled right-handed pitchers Emmet Sheehan and Kyle Hurt from Triple-A. Sheehan will take down bulk innings on Sunday as LA looks to preserve the bullpen heading into the final week of the regular season.
As for the corresponding moves, left-handed pitcher Tarik Skubal was placed on the bereavement list and will be away from the team for "a couple days," per manager Dave Roberts. Additionally, right-hander Seth Halvorsen was optioned.
Dodgers Recall Emmet Sheehan, Kyle Hurt
Sheehan was surprisingly demoted this past week amid a dominant stretch of play.
Across his last two starts at the MLB level, Sheehan allowed just one run over 11.2 innings with 15 strikeouts.
“Man, Emmet’s been great. The last two have been fantastic,” Roberts said after he was sent down. “Emmet’s done everything he can do in his power to force our hand, which I love. ... The last two have been really good.”
Now, Sheehan is getting another opportunity to take down bulk innings and audition for a spot on the postseason roster. If he has another strong outing, he'll likely secure a spot in the postseason bullpen as a multi-inning option.
As for Hurt, he's been up and down multiple times this season. The right-hander has made 43 appearances at the big league level, compiling a 4.33 ERA with 56 strikeouts to 23 walks over 43.2 innings of work.
He's unlikely to factor into the team's October plans, but could take down innings over the final week of the regular season.
Dodgers Place Tarik Skubal on Bereavement List, Option Seth Halvorsen
Skubal will deal with a personal matter for the next couple days, but should be back in time to make one more start before the conclusion of the regular season.
He pitched on Saturday, allowing four runs over five innings with three strikeouts.
As for Halvorsen, he's made 11 appearances at the big league level for the Dodgers this season, accruing an 8.10 ERA with six strikeouts to two walks over 10 innings of work.
He was acquired by the Dodgers a couple weeks before the trade deadline in a three-player deal with the Colorado Rockies. He likely won't return to the big league club for the remainder of the year.

item.dc:creator: Evan Roberts

As a fan, it's easy to just look at the starting unit of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, and Shohei Ohtani as one. But Yamamoto's latest feat stands out even relative to this dominant group of pitchers. Dodgers starter Yoshinobu Yamamoto has been dominant this season Yamamoto's most recent start came on S
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers starting rotation is so good collectively when they are healthy that it's sometimes difficult to focus on the individuals' accomplishments.
As a fan, it's easy to just look at the starting unit of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, and Shohei Ohtani as one. But Yamamoto's latest feat stands out even relative to this dominant group of pitchers.
Dodgers starter Yoshinobu Yamamoto has been dominant this season
Yamamoto's most recent start came on September 15 against the Cincinnati Reds at Great American Ball Park. It was yet another ho-hum performance by the Dodgers ace. He picked up the win going seven scoreless innings, while allowing just one hit. He only walked two batters while striking out seven. Yamamoto lowered his career WHIP to 0.96, which is officially the best WHIP ever by a pitcher their first 75 career starts.
Yamamoto outpaced 2025 National League Cy Young Award-winner — and perhaps future Dodgers pitcher in Paul Skenes — as well as former member of LA's pitching staff, Walker Buehler. Behind Yamamoto, Skenes, and Buehler are Seattle Mariners All-Star starter Bryan Woo and Tampa Bay Rays right-hander Drew Rasmussen.
Not only does Yamamoto have the best WHIP ever through his first 75 games, but he's allowed the third-fewest runs in MLB history by a pitcher through that same span (trailing only Rasmussen and Skenes).
Opposing hitters are hitting .192/.252/.310 against Yamamoto through those 75 starts -- that is the lowest batting average against of any pitcher since 1974 (when that data became available). It's also the lowest on-base percentage, the fifth-lowest slugging percentage, and the second-lowest OPS.
Below is a list of fewest hits allowed in MLB history by a pitcher in their first 75 starts. There's a lot of familiar names on that list.
| Pitcher | Hits Allowed |
|---|---|
| 1. Tony Gonsolin (LAD) | 264 |
| 2. Freddy Peralta (MIL) | 270 |
| 3. Drew Rasmussen (TB) | 284 |
| T-4. Cristian Javier (HOU) | 287 |
| T-4. Edward Cabrera (MIA) | 287 |
| 6. Triston McKenzie (CLE) | 295 |
| 7. Jack Flaherty (STL) | 299 |
| T-8. Yoshinobu Yamamoto (LAD) | 305 |
| T-8. Shohei Ohtani (LAA) | 305 |
| 10. Tyler Glasnow (LAD) | 313 |
Yamamoto has clearly been worth every penny since he signed that mega-deal with the Dodgers. It's nice to be able to point to his historic regular season success as well as his historic postseason success. Yamamoto is slowly building up a Hall of Fame résumé through his first three Major League seasons.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers doblegan Giants
Mookie Betts batea de 4-4 con tres triples y dos impulsadas
El novato dominicano Josué De Paula pega sencillo impulsador de 2 carreras, anota dos y recibe dos bases por bolas
LOS ÁNGELES.— Mookie Betts bateó de 4-4 con tres dobles, Will Smith agregó tres hits, incluyendo un jonrón, y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles vencieron a los Gigantes de San Francisco 10-4 el sábado por la noche.
El sencillo de dos carreras con dos outs de Tommy Edman ante el relevista Philip Abner rompió el empate a 4 en la quinta entrada. El bateador emergente Miguel Rojas conectó un sencillo productor para poner el marcador 7-4 a favor de su equipo, y Edman fue puesto out en el plato para finalizar la entrada.
Todos los Dodgers conectaron al menos un hit, excepto Freddie Freeman, quien tuvo un mal desempeño y se fue de 0 de 5. Betts igualó su mejor marca de la temporada en hits y el equipo superó a los Giants en jonrones, 15-8. El ex Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Americana bateaba .249 hace una semana y desde entonces ha elevado su promedio a .261.
Los Dodgers anotaron carreras en seis entradas consecutivas al inicio de un partido por primera vez en 10 años. Han anotado 15 carreras en sus últimas siete entradas ofensivas, incluyendo cuatro jonrones en la octava entrada contra Abner en el primer partido de la serie del viernes.
Los campeones de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional (95-60) ganaron su partido número 95 para colocarse 35 juegos por encima del .500, su mejor marca de la temporada.
El tercer doble de Betts abrió la sexta entrada y anotó con un sencillo productor de Smith ante el relevista Joel Kuhnel. El novato Josue De Paula añadió un sencillo productor de dos carreras, ampliando la ventaja a 10-4.
En tres ocasiones, los Giants remontaron para empatar el partido, solo para ver cómo los Dodgers volvían a tomar la delantera, destacando el jonrón de dos carreras de Victor Bericoto, de 425 pies, que empató el partido en la tercera entrada.
El abridor de los Dodgers, Tarik Skubal (11-7), no estuvo especialmente brillante, permitiendo cuatro carreras y ocho hits en cinco entradas. El zurdo ponchó a tres y otorgó dos bases por bolas, y los Dodgers ganaron sus últimas seis salidas.
El relevista Edwin Díaz lanzó una octava entrada sin permitir carreras en su segunda aparición consecutiva desde que salió de la lista de lesionados el viernes.
El abridor de los Giants, Yunior Marte (0-1), permitió seis carreras y ocho hits en 4 2/3 entradas con dos ponches.
El jardinero derecho de los Dodgers, Kyle Tucker, recibió un foul en la rodilla y fue reemplazado por Alex Call en la séptima entrada.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 10-4, on Saturday night and improved to 95-60 on the year.
Left-hander Tarik Skubal had an uncharacteristic start, striking out just three batters over five innings while allowing four earned runs. Fortunately, the bullpen picked him up with four scoreless innings.
Offensively, Mookie Betts had a marvelous four-hit night and Will Smith notched three hits of his own, including a home run. Rookie Josue De Paula continued to impress with two walks and a two-run single with the bases loaded.
After the game, manager Dave Roberts provided an update on Shohei Ohtani, saying he has a "good chance" of being activated during the team's series against the San Diego Padres this week.
While Ohtani is eligible to be activated on Wednesday, it's currently unclear if that's the day he'll be back.
Either way, the Dodgers are expecting Ohtani back soon, and he took a major step on Saturday, hitting off the Trajekt machine and running the bases before the game.
In his stead, De Paula has done an unbelievable job as the everyday designated hitter.
In other news, the Dodgers recently promoted an outfielder who previously thought that his season might be over. The third-round pick in the 2024 MLB Draft was hitting .306 with a .985 OPS across 35 games in High-A and 71 appearances in Double-A this season.
Finally, veteran outfielder Teoscar Hernández was recently labeled as a likely trade candidate by Pat Ragazzo of FanSided. The insider explained that the influx of outfield talent, combined with an expiring contract that was reportedly being shopped around over the offseason, could lead to the team parting ways with "Mr. Seeds."
"The Dodgers have No. 1 prospect Josue De Paula and other young outfielders in their farm system, who could replace Hernandez in left field next season," Ragazzo wrote. "It would make sense for the Dodgers to ship Hernandez out this offseason with one-year remaining on his deal."

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have done it again.
With the Dodgers’ win on Thursday afternoon, they officially clinched the NL West championship for the fifth consecutive year. This marks the Dodgers’ 13th NL West title out of the past 14 years, with their lone second place finish coming in 2021 behind an otherworldly season from the San Francisco Giants.
It has been an interesting season for this Dodgers team. After a scorching hot 56-30 start through June, the Dodgers slumped to a 26-25 record in July and August. Now hunting for the top seed in the National League for the postseason, the Dodgers have bounced back to an 11-5 record in September (as of Thursday).
A major factor in the Dodgers’ volatility this year has been their susceptibility to injury. This year alone, a whopping 27 players have seen time on the Dodgers’ injured list.
The majority of these players have made their way back from the injured list, to varying degrees of success. Of those who have returned to the active roster, one player stands above them all.
Starter Blake Snell has been on a tear since his return from the injured list. While his status moving forward is now in question following his early exit from his September 16 start against the Cincinnati Reds, his run of dominance has been a sight to behold.
Yet, for Snell, the journey to get to this point has been far from a walk in the park.
Stats as of September 17.
Celebrations and Setbacks
Snell came into the 2026 season as arguably the co-ace of the Dodgers’ starting rotation, alongside Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
The left-hander had been a pivotal part of the Dodgers’ 2025 World Series run, allowing just two runs over his first 21 innings of work. Snell cooled off significantly in the World Series, allowing 10 earned runs over 13 innings, but he was invaluable to the Dodgers nonetheless.
However, Snell’s heavy usage in October had some untoward downstream effects. Left with minimal recovery time between the end of the season and the beginning of spring training, Snell had difficulty getting ramped back up for the year. As a result, his offseason throwing progression suffered unanticipated delays.
Lingering shoulder fatigue kept Snell off of the mound through early May, missing the first 38 games. Finally, nearly a month and a half into the 2026 season, Snell was set to make his season debut. Unfortunately for Snell and the Dodgers, his return was interrupted almost immediately.
After three innings against the Atlanta Braves on May 9, Snell’s season debut was done. He allowed four earned runs, striking out five batters while allowing six hits and two walks. Unbeknownst to Snell, this would be his last start for over three months.
Snell was scratched from his next scheduled start. Just one day later, he underwent surgery to remove loose bodies from his left elbow. As a result, Snell missed another 78 games, finally making his return in early August. Since then, he seems to have unlocked a new level.
Second-Half Hero
Snell has long been known to elevate his game during the second half of each season. For his career, he has posted a 3.96 ERA in the first half and a 2.31 ERA during the latter half. As good as his career second-half numbers may be, he’s been even better in his return to the mound this year.
Over his last seven starts, Snell has pitched to an incredible 1.01 ERA, recording 47 strikeouts and 14 walks over 35.2 innings. Opponents are batting a measly .164/.254/.205 against him, and he has allowed no more than one run in any start during this span.
With a sample this small, it is difficult to quantify just how effective Snell has been compared to his Dodgers teammates. This is especially true given the run their starting rotation has been on in recent weeks.
Both Yamamoto and the Dodgers’ marquee trade deadline pickup, Tarik Skubal, have been dominant in their own right. Since Snell returned to the rotation on August 11, Yamamoto and Skubal have each posted an ERA under 2.10 over 30+ innings apiece.
Still, Snell’s ERA over the same span clears both of theirs by a full run. Though Skubal narrowly edges out Snell in fWAR (1.8 fWAR vs. 1.7 fWAR), Snell’s success is all the more unprecedented given this is his first sustained stretch of play since the 2025 postseason.
Expanding beyond just the Dodgers, Snell’s metrics stack up well among the league’s best. Among all qualified pitchers over the same span, Snell holds the second-best ERA, third-best FIP, second-best fWAR, and third-best K/9 rate. He is the only qualified pitcher to have yet to surrender a home run over this span.
What’s Been Working?
Since returning from the IL, Snell has demonstrated a number of improvements.
For one, his stuff seems to have jumped in effectiveness. Every one of Snell’s pitches has seen either a marginal or significant jump in induced movement.
In particular, his fastball has gained nearly an inch of both induced vertical break and horizontal break. This pairs incredibly well with his improved curveball, which has gained two inches of depth and over an inch of horizontal movement.
Factoring in his slider and changeup, Snell’s arsenal has looked remarkably effective as a whole. As a result, his two best pitches have played up in a big way. Though the sample is small, Snell’s fastball has allowed just a 5.6% hard-hit percentage. While batters hit .309 and slugged .426 against his heater in 2025, those figures have dropped to .179 and .232 so far this year.
The results on his curveball have been even more effective, as batters are batting and slugging .086 against it. In 37 plate appearances, hitters have recorded just three hits against Snell’s curveball compared to 20 strikeouts. He has yet to allow an extra-base hit with his curveball in 2026.
Beyond Snell’s improved arsenal, he has also located the ball well. A pitcher with Snell’s profile traditionally operates best working around the edges of the strike zone. This allows him to induce whiffs and chase swings, leading to a higher strikeout rate and more frequent weak contact, but also more walks.
Snell has leaned into this philosophy, attacking early while working around the edges later in at-bats. He has thrown fewer balls in the zone overall, improving his chase rate, but has also significantly increased his first-pitch strike percentage.
Room for Concern
Snell’s run of dominance has been impressive, to say the least. But, his most recent start brings a sobering point to the conversation around his performance.
Last year, the Dodgers leaned heavily on Snell at the end of the regular season and the postseason. He did not bounce back gracefully, missing over 100 games in the 2026 season.
This year, the Dodgers hope to lean on Snell heavily once again as they approach October baseball. As such, it is reasonable to air concerns around the volatility of his health, with his most recent start as an example.
Snell left after one inning against the Reds, citing a left groin issue. In years past, Snell has missed anywhere from a few weeks to a couple of months battling the same issue.
However, he did frame his decision to exit the game as precautionary, rather than reactive. According to Snell, he felt the area tighten up during his pre-game bullpen, and he felt it was best not to push it. While he still hopes to make his next start, nobody can know for sure what the full impact of this issue will wind up being.
The Dodgers have yet to make any further announcements around the injury. At this time, Snell has not been placed on the injured list either. The first real test will be whether Snell ends up making his next start. Manager Dave Roberts has weighed the idea of delaying it, but any deviation from the norm will have an impact at this stage.
Whether Snell remains healthy through October is anybody’s guess. Regardless, his remarkable performance since coming back from injury is a testament to both his talent and resilience. Hopefully, fans can look forward to Snell making a comeback against the San Diego Padres next week.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

20 Sep 2026, 13:49 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Arianna Grainey)
Pinch hitter Pavin Smith hit a two-run, walk-off homer with one out in the ninth and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 5-3 on Saturday in Phoenix on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series victory over the Yankees.
Ildemaro Vargas walked to lead off the ninth off Michael Fulmer (0-1), reaching base after he appealed the 3-2 pitch that originally was called a strike. After a strikeout, Smith hit a 391-foot homer to right center for the D-backs' 46th comeback win of the season
Heliot Ramos and Austin Wells hit bases-empty homers for the Yankees, who had won four of five and eight of 10. Wells and Jose Caballero had two hits apiece.
Nolan Arenado had two hits and Jordan Lawlar added a two-run triple for the D-backs, who had lost three in a row and five of six.
The Yankees (89-65), who have clinched a playoff berth, fell five games behind Tampa Bay (94-60) in the American League East and remained 5 1/2 games ahead of Boston (84-71) for the top AL wild-card spot. The Yankees and Rays play a four-game series in Yankee Stadium beginning with a split doubleheader Tuesday.
White Sox 3, Tigers 1
Sean Burke hurled six quality innings and Miguel Vargas homered to help Chicago earn a victory over visiting Detroit.
Burke (10-7) allowed one run on five hits for Chicago, which remained a game behind American League Central-leading Cleveland. Sam Antonacci and Munetaka Murakami both drove in a run and Grant Taylor delivered a four-out save, his 10th overall this season.
Jackson Jobe (2-3) threw six innings of three-run, four-hit ball, striking out nine for Detroit, which remains barely alive in AL Central contention. The Tigers' wild-card elimination magic number is down to one. Kevin McGonigle drove in Detroit's lone run.
Mets 10, Phillies 3
Francisco Alvarez had two hits, including the go-ahead three-run homer in the fifth, as host New York routed skidding Philadelphia.
Carson Benge was 3-for-4 with a solo homer and two RBIs for the Mets. Brett Baty had two hits, including a run-scoring single, while Benge, Juan Soto and Bo Bichette each had RBI singles during a four-run eighth.
Alec Bohm had RBI singles in the fourth and fifth for the Phillies, who missed a chance to take over the top National League wild card, at least temporarily. The Cubs and Padres both won to remain tied atop the NL wild-card race.
Brewers 1, Orioles 0Robert Gasser pitched seven shutout innings as the first of three Milwaukee pitchers in a victory against host Baltimore.
It marked the second shutout for Milwaukee pitchers in an eight-game stretch, needing only four strikeouts for the latest accomplishment. The Brewers scored on Gary Sanchez's second-inning groundout to knock in Joey Ortiz, who tripled with one out.Baltimore has lost the first two games of the series following a three-game winning streak, further damaging its American League playoff hopes. Orioles starter Trevor Rogers (10-11) lasted eight innings, allowing one run and three hits.
Rangers 6, Blue Jays 2Texas won for the sixth time in its past seven games, defeating Toronto in Arlington, Texas.Rangers starting pitcher Cal Quantrill left the game after 1 1/3 innings with right lat tightness. Jordan Montgomery (1-0) replaced him and held Toronto hitless through 3 2/3 innings. Josh Jung gave Texas a 1-0 lead in the bottom of the first with a home run to right field.Jose Soriano (12-8) gave up six runs (five earned) on four hits and struck out eight in five-plus innings for the Blue Jays, who dropped to three games behind the Chicago White Sox for the final wild-card berth in the American League.
Rays 2, Red Sox 1
Richie Palacios produced a two-out, walk-off single in the ninth inning as Tampa Bay edged Boston in St. Petersburg, Fla., to even their final home series of the regular season.
Against Garrett Whitlock (7-2), Palacios looped a 1-2 sinker into right to score Junior Caminero as the Rays hit their third walk-off winner during their nine-game homestand. Jonathan Aranda homered while Liam Hicks and Chandler Simpson posted two hits apiece.
Caleb Durbin stroked two doubles and scored for the Red Sox, who lost for the first time in three games. Starting pitcher Brayan Bello went a season-best eight innings and allowed one run on five hits with a career high-tying 11 strikeouts.
Guardians 12, Athletics 6
Angel Martinez homered from both sides of the plate and drove in four runs in host Cleveland's win over the Athletics which helped maintain its one-game lead in the American League Central.
Martinez was also 4-for-5 with a double and three runs scored and Chase DeLauter also homered for the Guardians, who won their fourth straight. Slade Cecconi (5-7) got the win in relief with two scoreless innings after Tanner Bibee lasted 4 2/3 innings and surrendered six runs on 12 hits.
Donovan Walton hit a home run and was 3-for-3 with four RBIs for the Athletics, who have lost five in a row. Athletics starter and loser Jacob Lopez (6-5) was blitzed for 10 runs and 10 hits in 2 2/3 innings.
Nationals 8, Cardinals 5 (11 innings)Jose Tena's two-run double keyed a four-run 11th inning and Washington beat the Cardinals in St. Louis.Jorbit Vivas had four hits and Daylen Lile homered for Washington, which has won six of seven. Riley Cornelio (3-2) pitched 1 2/3 innings for the win.At the top of the order, Jose Fermin and Ivan Herrera had three hits each for St. Louis, which has lost four straight.
Cubs 5, Reds 2
Michael Busch and Dansby Swanson hit solo home runs to lift visiting Chicago to a win over Cincinnati.
The win allowed the Cubs to pull a full game ahead of the Philadelphia Phillies for the top wild-card playoff spot in the National League. The Phillies lost 10-3 to the Mets earlier. The San Diego Padres also won to remain tied with the Cubs.
The teams will play the rubber game of the series Sunday. Cubs starter Matthew Boyd (9-5) gave up two hits and two runs (one earned) in five innings. Reds starter Nick Lodolo (3-6) gave up seven hits and three runs in seven innings.
Pirates 6, Royals 5
Brandon Lowe launched a go-ahead two-run home run in the eighth inning to power Pittsburgh to a victory over visiting Kansas City.
Ronny Simon and Jake Mangum each hit two-run homers, while Oneil Cruz, Rafael Flores Jr. and Lowe each had two hits for the Pirates. Right-hander Luke Weaver (3-1) threw a scoreless eighth with one strikeout, and left-hander Mason Montgomery earned his 15th save of the season after working around a walk with one strikeout in a scoreless ninth.
Nick Loftin had four hits, while Bobby Witt Jr. went 3-for-5 with two runs and extended his on-base streak to 17 games for the Royals. Carter Jensen hit a solo homer, while Jac Caglianone and Vinnie Pasquantino each had two hits for Kansas City.
Braves 6, Astros 3Ronald Acuna Jr. hit a grand slam, Grant Holmes produced a quality start and Atlanta lowered its magic number to one to clinch the National League East by defeating host Houston.The Braves secured this three-game interleague series and set the table to win the NL East for the seventh time in nine seasons with a victory in the series finale on Sunday. Holmes (10-5) allowed two runs on eight hits over six innings. Closer Raisel Iglesias notched his 34th save for Atlanta.The Astros dropped a game behind the Rangers in the AL West after Texas beat Toronto. Astros reliever AJ Blubaugh (5-3) loaded the bases and was replaced by Bryan Abreu, who gave up Acuna's homer in the seventh inning for a 5-2 Braves lead.Rockies 5, Mariners 3
Cole Carrigg delivered a go-ahead two-run single in a four-run seventh inning as Colorado edged Seattle in Denver.
Juan Mejia (4-6) pitched two scoreless innings and Brennan Bernardino got the final three outs for his second save for Colorado. Jake McCarthy and TJ Rumfield each produced an RBI.
Cal Raleigh and Randy Arozarena homered and Julio Rodriguez and Michael Arroyo had two hits each for Seattle, which is on the brink of elimination in the AL wild-card race.
Padres 6, Marlins 5 (10 innings)
Rookie Ethan Salas stroked an RBI single in the bottom of the 10th inning and San Diego edged visiting Miami.
Salas' hit scored Jake Cronenworth, who started the inning as the automatic runner at second base and advanced to third on a wild pitch by Josh Ekness (2-4). David Morgan (4-1) stranded runners at first and second in the top of the 10th to earn the win, San Diego's 12th in 13 games.
The Padres tied the Chicago Cubs for the top wild-card spot in the National League at 86-69. Miami forced extra innings when pinch hitter Griffin Conine pulled a 102 mph fastball from closer Mason Miller for a game-tying homer with one out in the ninth.
Dodgers 10, Giants 4
Mookie Betts tied a season high with four hits, Tommy Edman delivered a go-ahead two-run single and Los Angeles stayed within two games of the best record in the National League with a victory over visiting San Francisco.
Betts has 10 hits over his past three games, including seven in the past two while operating out of the leadoff spot in place of an injured Shohei Ohtani. Will Smith homered as the Dodgers won for the fifth time in six games and improved to 13-3 since Sept. 3. Tarik Skubal (11-7) gave up four runs on eight hits over five innings.
Victor Bericoto hit a home run among his two hits for the Giants while Yunior Marte (0-1) gave up six runs on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings in his fourth career appearance and second start.
Angels 6, Twins 5 (11 innings)Christian Moore singled in automatic runner Zach Neto with a bases-loaded comebacker off pitcher Taylor Rogers' leg with two outs in the bottom of the 11th inning as Los Angeles edged Minnesota in Anaheim, Calif.Moore drilled a first-pitch sweeper that caromed off the leg of Rogers (6-4) and back toward the third base line as Neto sprinted home. Tayler Saucedo (1-1) struck out two during a scoreless inning of relief for the Angels, who tied it at 5-5 in the bottom of the ninth on Vaughn Grissom's homer.Ryan Kreidler hit a home run, Victor Caratini went 2-for-5 with two RBIs, Walker Jenkins had two hits and a run and Josh Bell and Royce Lewis each had two hits for the Twins.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [True Blue LA] With the season winding down, Mookie Betts is heating up
item.dc:creator: Jacob Macofsky

item.content:encoded:
2026 looked to be a lost season for Mookie Betts, as an oblique injury cost him a month’s worth of time. At the All-Star break, the Dodgers shortstop was limping to the tune of a .235/.293/.416 slashline with 11 home runs and 31 RBI over 60 games.
Since the second half of the regular season began, Betts has turned into his 2023 MVP-runner-up self, as he’s slashing .290/.364/.452 with 11 home runs and 36 RBI over his last 56 games. Betts has been on a tear his last three games, as he’s hitting .833 with five extra-base hits and five RBI, highlighted by a four-hit, three-double game on Saturday in the Dodgers’ 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants.
Betts has hit all around the lineup, going from as high as leadoff to as low as the six hole, but Betts has been certifying himself as a force at the top of the lineup during this final homestand. Betts spoke with David Vassegh of SportsNet LA about his torrid stretch at the plate hitting at the top spot following Saturday’s win, noting that the return of Shohei Ohtani will directly impact where he hits everyday.
“It’s fun. Like you said, I’ve done it for so long, but that man Shohei— he deserves what he gets. We all know where he needs to hit in the lineup.”
Saturday was a rough outing for left-hander Tarik Skubal as he allowed four earned runs while striking out a season-low three hitters over five innings.
Despite the atypical night for Skubal, his offense was able to generate six runs after his final pitch, giving him his fourth win as a Dodger. When speaking with Vassegh following the game, Skubal gave all the credit to the offense and bullpen for carrying the team the rest of the way.
“Obviously, I wasn’t very good today. The offense, defense and bullpen picked me up big time, and that’s what good teams do— they pick each other up, and win series and win baseball games. Hats off to them.”
Mirjam Swanson at the Los Angeles Times writes about Tyler Glasnow and the ability to trust himself as the playoffs loom near. Glasnow was solid on Friday against San Francisco, allowing just two runs while striking out 10 hitters.
“Today was a step in the right direction,” said Glasnow, the formerHart High star, before leaving the clubhouse in flip-flops. “I’d rather kind of feel it, work through some stuff, and have a good one right before playoffs.
“I think I’m in a good spot right now.”
Jack Harris of the California Post has a positive update regarding Shohei Ohtani, as the two-way superstar did base running drills and used the Trajekt Ark pitching machine in the cage. Hitting coach Aaron Bates notes that Ohtani has been really good with the machine, and the next test will be how he performs in live batting practice.
“In the cage, in a controlled setting, he’s been really good. It’s 100% intensity,” Bates said. “Once he gets out to the field, if he does a live BP or something like that, and the intensity ramps up, it’ll be a good test to see what happens. But in the cage, in the controlled setting, he’s been really good.”

item.title: [pasadenastarnews.com] Mookie Betts stays hot as Dodgers hammer Giants
item.dc:creator: Doug Padilla
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Mookie Betts is showing that the view from the top offers a wide range of possibilities. Hitting in Shohei Ohtani’s leadoff spot for the second consecutive game, Betts’ four-hit performance on Saturday night topped his three-hit output from Friday and started some serious downhill momentum toward a 10-4 victory over the San Francisco Giants. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Mookie Betts is showing that the view from the top offers a wide range of possibilities.
Hitting in Shohei Ohtani’s leadoff spot for the second consecutive game, Betts’ four-hit performance on Saturday night topped his three-hit output from Friday and started some serious downhill momentum toward a 10-4 victory over the San Francisco Giants.
The victory kept the Dodgers (95-60) two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers (97-58) for the best record in the National League and four games ahead of the Atlanta Braves (91-64) for the No. 2 playoff seed with seven games remaining. That includes four games against the Giants, who continue to limp toward the finish line of a miserable, injury-riddled season.
Betts couldn’t be feeling better, with his past two games part of a run of 10 hits over the last three games he has played. After more than two months of looking for an offensive leader, Betts has charged into the role, while reaching base five times on Saturday.
“It’s good; It’s fun,” Betts said. “But the main thing is doing it when it counts. So right now, we just keep laying the foundation, and then when playoffs come, we just need it to show up (offensively).”
The Dodgers expect Ohtani to return for the playoffs as he makes progress from biceps and knee discomfort. Betts, though, is proving to be a more-than-adequate emergency replacement.
“You know, I couldn’t tell you that I saw this (coming), but I just felt that he was stronger,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s worked hard on that. He looks great. He’s not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great, and I think for me it’s just trying to keep him confident.”
The Dodgers also have been transformed by the emergence of catcher Will Smith, who returned at the start of September after three months away because of neck inflammation. He had a home run among his three hits Saturday to give him homers in consecutive games, with three over his past eight contests.
“He’ll play two or three that last series (at San Francisco), but yeah, after that, he’ll be our guy (for the playoffs),” Roberts said.
There is also 21-year-old rookie Josue De Paula, who has continued to operate with ease since arriving in the major leagues last week. De Paula had a two-run single Saturday and walked twice while scoring two runs.
All of it overshadowed Tarik Skubal’s ninth start for the Dodgers. The two-time American League Cy Young Award winner was far from his best, allowing four runs on eight hits over five innings. His three strikeouts were his least in an outing with his new club.
Skubal unleashed his frustrations in the dugout by throwing his glove and cap at the bench, while firing an empty sports drink bottle at the wall.
“Sometimes you get frustrated and you got to get it out,” Skubal said. “It’s no good just keeping it pent up. So yeah, I’m a believer in getting that stuff out and kind of just moving on from the moment. The frustration is based on execution and knowing who I am and I’m just not doing that.”
Skubal blamed a lack of fastball command for the inability to shut down the Giants.
“Not driving it up and in (and) kind of pulling the ball down at times, pushing it up at times,” Skubal said. “I think pitching is almost all fastball command and mine wasn’t great today.”
And yet the offense allowed Skubal (11-7) to pick up the win, while improving to 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA for the Dodgers.
“That’s our job. That’s what we’re supposed to do,” Betts said. “So sometimes it’s them, sometimes it’s us. As long as we win.”
Kyle Tucker provided a scare when he fouled a ball off the side of his right knee early in the game then departed in the seventh inning with the Dodgers leading by six runs. Tucker reached base twice Saturday after collecting six hits with two home runs the previous two games.
“Whatever’s working at the time, you just ride it out, whether or not it’s the way you want to go about it,” said Tucker, who expects to play Sunday. “If it’s working, it’s working. You just try to go up there and put up competitive at-bats and just do your part on defense.”
The offense was not only productive, it was steady. The Dodgers scored runs in each of the first six innings and when they were held scoreless in the seventh, Betts still reached base with a walk.
Betts opened the game for the Dodgers with a leadoff double and scored on a Max Muncy double. Betts brought home his own run with an RBI single in the second.
The Dodgers struck with Smith’s home run in the third and got an RBI double from Betts in the fourth but were still tied 4-4 heading into the bottom of the fifth. They blew the game open from there, getting a go-ahead two-run single from Tommy Edman and an RBI pinch-hit single from Miguel Rojas for a 7-4 lead.
They scored three more times in the sixth, getting a Smith RBI single followed by a two-run single from De Paula.
“I think this is the first time, seems like all year, that we’ve had four or five hitters swing the bats well for four or five games,” Roberts said. “So it’s been really good to see. Obviously, Mookie is a big part of it, but everyone else is doing their part.”
The Dodgers now have a 5-4 lead in the Giants in the season series and are in line for a sweep on Sunday, which would be their first against their longtime rival since April of 2024.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers outslug Giants 10-4, led by Mookie Betts with four hits
Mookie Betts had four hits, including three doubles, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 10-4
LOS ANGELES -- Mookie Betts went 4 for 4 with three doubles, Will Smith added three hits including a home run, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 10-4 on Saturday night.
Tommy Edman's two-run, two-out single off reliever Philip Abner snapped a 4-all tie in the fifth. Pinch-hitter Miguel Rojas followed with an RBI single for a 7-4 lead, with Edman thrown out at home to end the inning.
Every Dodger had at least one hit, except for struggling Freddie Freeman who was 0 for 5. Betts tied his season high for hits and the team outslugged the Giants, 15-8. The former AL MVP was hitting .249 a week ago, and has since raised his average to .261.
The Dodgers scored runs in six straight innings to start a game for the first time in 10 years. They've scored 15 runs in their last seven offensive innings, including a four-homer eighth off Abner in Friday's series opener.
The NL West champions (95-60) won their 95th game to move a season-high 35 games above .500.
Betts' third double led off the sixth and he scored on Smith's RBI single off reliever Joel Kuhnel. Rookie Josue De Paula added a two-run RBI single, extending the lead to 10-4.
Three times the Giants rallied to tie the game only to see the Dodgers retake the lead, highlighted by Victor Bericoto's game-tying, 425-foot two-run homer in the third.
Dodgers starter Tarik Skubal (11-7) wasn't particularly sharp, allowing four runs and eight hits in five innings. The left-hander struck out three and walked two, with the Dodgers winning each of his last six outings.
Reliever Edwin Díaz pitched a scoreless eighth in his second straight appearance since coming off the injured list Friday.
Giants starter Yunior Marte (0-1) gave up six runs and eight hits in 4 2/3 innings with two strikeouts.
Dodgers right fielder Kyle Tucker fouled a ball off his knee and was replaced by Alex Call in the seventh.
Neither team had announced their starters for the series finale Sunday.

item.title: [bignewsnetwork.com] Mookie Betts, Dodgers stay hot in romp over Giants
